ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Event, TargetType.AllEnemies)` (Exterminate.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / ATTACK / EVENT / ALL_ENEMIES. `handles_own_routing = True` is faithful for the same reason as conflagration's: C#'s OnPlay runs once and the multi-hit fan-out happens inside the attack command.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(3m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new RepeatVar(4)` (Exterminate.cs:13-17) == both numbers, and `base_hits` reports 4.

OnPlay.issue: Damage per hit, hit count, target set and the hits-outer/enemies-inner loop order are all faithful against `DamageCmd.Attack(3).WithHitCount(4).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` (Exterminate.cs:26-29) -- AttackCommand runs `for (i = 0; i < attackCount; i++)` with the target list re-derived per hit (AttackCommand.cs:538-546), and the sim's `for _ in range(self._hits)` with a fresh `is_gone` filter per hit matches. ALL-ENEMIES FAN-OUT: C# passes the whole valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets)` call per hit (AttackCommand.cs:650), which computes every target's DamageResult first, runs the after-damage hooks over all of them, and only then calls `await Kill(killedCreatures)` for the batch (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409). The sim issues a SEPARATE `DamageCmd.deal` per enemy, so each death and its on-death effects fully resolve before the next enemy is damaged. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/conflagration's OnPlay entry (rule 3). DORMANT: no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage or block, so both orders reach the same end state. Live the moment such a monster is ported.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Exterminate.cs:34) == `self._damage += 1` (3 -> 4). The REPEAT count stays 4 when upgraded -- the opposite of card/conflagration, whose upgrade raises the repeat and leaves the damage. Both checked against their own sources rather than assumed from the pattern.

guards.what: the sim checks `_all_enemies_dead() or player.is_dead` AFTER each full sweep; C# checks `validTargets.Count == 0` and `Attacker.IsDead` at the START of each hit (event_cards.py:237-238 vs AttackCommand.cs:540-550)
guards.rationale: Equivalent: an empty living-enemy list at the top of the sim's next hit would skip every `DamageCmd.deal` anyway (the `is_gone` continue), so the explicit break only saves work. Both stop fanning out once the player has died mid-attack.
